sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's almost like a monument to the possibility that we could preserve something where, like, as a, like, what to put in there was an afterthought.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是一个纪念碑，纪念我们能够保存某些东西的可能性，而至于放什么进去，反而是事后才想到的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So what would have been interesting?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么东西会更有趣呢？

sentences.en: What could she put in there that you as a historian, and you particularly as like an archive nut, as the type of historian who likes old dusty things to pull out, like,
sentences.zh: 她可以放些什么进去，让你作为一个历史学家，特别是作为一个档案狂，作为一个喜欢挖掘尘封旧物的历史学家，你会，

sentences.en: what would you have liked to have seen?
sentences.zh: 你希望看到什么？

sentences.en: Oh, something totally sneaky.
sentences.zh: 哦，一些非常隐秘的东西。

sentences.en: First of all, nothing published, nothing that is not handwritten or hand drawn, like the, something that is one of a kind that exists nowhere else, that can be found nowhere else,
sentences.zh: 首先，不能是任何出版物，不能是任何非手写或非手绘的东西，比如，那种独一无二、别处不存在、无法在其他地方找到的东西，

sentences.en: that would be a revelation upon its discovery.
sentences.zh: 那种一旦被发现就会带来启示的东西。

sentences.en: So, love letters of Ulysses S.
sentences.zh: 所以，尤利西斯·S·

sentences.en: Grant, I don't know, you know, like, I don't really care about Ulysses S.
sentences.zh: 格兰特的情书，我不知道，你知道，我其实并不关心尤利西斯·S·

sentences.en: Grant.
sentences.zh: 格兰特。

sentences.en: But the diary of a Chinese railroad worker who was learning English or something, like, something that we don't have.
sentences.zh: 但如果是一位正在学习英语的中国铁路工人的日记之类的，那种我们没有的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And that we were not, that was not going to survive otherwise.
sentences.zh: 而且我们如果不这样做，它就不会流传下来的东西。

sentences.en: I very much take Jill's point here.
sentences.zh: 我非常赞同吉尔的观点。

sentences.en: I can't imagine how disappointing everything in the safe must have felt after 100 years of buildup.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象在经历了100年的铺垫后，保险箱里的一切会让人感到多么失望。

sentences.en: But I will say, even those objects that seem like they are absolutely worthless, when you spend a little bit of time with them, they do take you somewhere.
sentences.zh: 但我还是要说，即使是那些看起来毫无价值的物品，当你花点时间去研究它们时，它们确实能带你回到过去。

sentences.en: Like the temperance pamphlet.
sentences.zh: 比如那本禁酒宣传册。

sentences.en: Of course, a handwritten original item would be more profound.
sentences.zh: 当然，一份手写的原件会更深刻。

sentences.en: But this mass-printed pamphlet represents one of the biggest social movements at the time.
sentences.zh: 但这本大规模印刷的小册子代表了当时最大的社会运动之一。

sentences.en: One that would ultimately amend the Constitution, not once, but twice.
sentences.zh: 这一运动最终修正了宪法，而且不是一次，是两次。

sentences.en: This fight over alcohol that is so far in the past for us was front of mind for them.
sentences.zh: 这场关于酒精的斗争对我们来说已经非常遥远，但对他们来说却是当务之急。

sentences.en: Or that photograph of the 44th Congress.
sentences.zh: 或者那张第44届国会的照片。

sentences.en: It features eight black members, more than ever before.
sentences.zh: 它有八名黑人议员，比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: But it was also the last time we would have so many black representatives for almost 100 years.
sentences.zh: 但这也是我们在近100年里拥有最多黑人代表的最后一次。

sentences.en: Were they thinking at this moment in 1876 that this progress would continue?
sentences.zh: 他们在1876年的那一刻是否认为这种进步会持续下去？

sentences.en: Or could they feel the failure of Reconstruction on the horizon?
sentences.zh: 还是他们已经感受到了重建失败的阴影？

sentences.en: Even that thoroughly unremarkable inkwell that Ford pulled from the safe.
sentences.zh: 即使是福特从保险箱里拿出的那个平平无奇的墨水瓶。

sentences.en: It belonged to Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, the celebrated poet and author of Paul Revere's Ride.
sentences.zh: 它属于亨利·沃兹沃思·朗费罗，那位著名的诗人和《保罗·里维尔骑马》的作者。

sentences.en: He's the reason every American knows the Redcoats are coming.
sentences.zh: 正是因为他，每个美国人才知道“红衫军来了”。

sentences.en: The version of the Revolutionary War most people carry around in their heads came from his pen.
sentences.zh: 大多数美国人脑海中关于独立战争的版本都出自他的笔下。

sentences.en: But when the safe was filled, he was still deep in mourning from the death of his wife.
sentences.zh: 但当保险箱被填满时，他正深陷于丧妻之痛中。

sentences.en: She was at home with him when her dress caught fire.
sentences.zh: 当时她正和他在家，裙子突然着火了。

sentences.en: And when Longfellow tried to smother the flames, he suffered severe burns to his face.
sentences.zh: 当朗费罗试图扑灭火焰时，他的脸部受到了严重烧伤。

sentences.en: From then on, he wore a long beard to hide his scars.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，他留起了长胡子来遮盖伤疤。

sentences.en: He was never the same.
sentences.zh: 他再也不是以前的他了。

sentences.en: One writer said his poems about mourning effectively turned him into the nation's grief counselor.
sentences.zh: 一位作家说，他关于哀悼的诗歌实际上使他成为了国家的悲伤辅导员。

sentences.en: And the only reason I know all this is because that inkwell was in the century safe.
sentences.zh: 而我之所以知道这一切，仅仅是因为那个墨水瓶在世纪保险箱里。

sentences.en: So I understand the disappointment of Joe Lepore and President Ford
sentences.zh: 所以我理解乔·莱波雷和福特总统，

sentences.en: and the entire population of the United States in 1976.
sentences.zh: 以及1976年全体美国民众的失望。

sentences.en: But I do think that in all these objects, in any American object, you can find America.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，在所有这些物品中，在任何美国物品中，你都能找到美国。

sentences.en: The reason why I want to talk to you about this, about the century safe,
sentences.zh: 我之所以想和你谈谈这个，关于世纪保险箱，

sentences.en: is because we're embarking on this series called A History of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是因为我们正在开启一个名为《美国历史》的系列节目，

sentences.en: in 100 Objects.
sentences.zh: 通过100件物品讲述。

sentences.en: And so we're kind of picking things out, you know, to represent the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们正在挑选一些东西，你知道，来代表美国。

sentences.en: And I was just wondering, like, should we even be trying to do this?
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，我们真的应该尝试这样做吗？

sentences.en: Like, do you have some advice?
sentences.zh: 你有什么建议吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: I say go.
sentences.zh: 我说去做吧。

sentences.en: I say I'm glad you're doing it.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你在做这件事。

sentences.en: You will have fun.
sentences.zh: 你会乐在其中的。

sentences.en: I think that, um, I think it is important to recognize that much like the present,
sentences.zh: 我认为，嗯，我认为重要的是要认识到，就像现在一样，

sentences.en: the past is largely a chronicle of misery.
sentences.zh: 过去在很大程度上是一部苦难史。

sentences.en: I mean, people suffer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们在受苦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And the people who suffer the most leave the least evidence behind.
sentences.zh: 而受苦最深的人留下的证据最少。

sentences.en: And so any history that begins with what survives has a real challenge to arriving at any proper perspective on the human condition.
sentences.zh: 因此，任何从幸存物开始的历史，在对人类状况获得正确的视角方面都面临着真正的挑战。

sentences.en: I think of that as the asymmetry of the historical record, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是历史记录的不对称性，对吧？

sentences.en: The people who were wealthiest and most literate and had the greatest resources not only left,
sentences.zh: 那些最富有、受教育程度最高、拥有最多资源的人，不仅留下了，

sentences.en: not only made a lot of records, um, they managed to have their records preserved.
sentences.zh: 不仅留下了大量的记录，嗯，他们还设法保存了这些记录。

sentences.en: And everyone else disappears and just vanishes.
sentences.zh: 而其他人则消失了，彻底消失了。

sentences.en: Their remains are gone.
sentences.zh: 他们的遗迹荡然无存。

sentences.en: And I think it puts a special obligation in anyone who's trying to write history or tell a story about the past to be attentive,
sentences.zh: 我认为这给任何试图书写历史或讲述过去故事的人带来了一种特殊的义务，那就是要保持专注，

sentences.en: uh, to not give up in the face of the asymmetry and to try to repair the historical record by finding other kinds of evidence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不要在不对称性面前放弃，要尝试通过寻找其他种类的证据来修复历史记录。

sentences.en: Um, the evidence that does survive, um, that makes sure that we understand the lives, both of the powerful and the powerless.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那些确实幸存下来的证据，嗯，确保我们能够理解权势者和无权者的生活。

sentences.en: But I wouldn't fall into the notion that it is, um, that you're assembling, uh, an exquisite and representative archive.
sentences.zh: 但我不会陷入那种认为你正在组建一个精致且具有代表性的档案库的观念中。

sentences.en: We are not making an official archive.
sentences.zh: 我们不是在制作官方档案。

sentences.en: It probably won't be exquisite.
sentences.zh: 它可能不会很精致。

sentences.en: But we are going to tell our story.
sentences.zh: 但我们要讲述我们的故事。

sentences.en: The story of the United States through objects.
sentences.zh: 通过物品讲述美国的故事。

sentences.en: 100 objects, to be exact.
sentences.zh: 准确地说是100件物品。

sentences.en: We are going to try to look beyond the official record, outside of the things we've already thought to preserve and put behind museum glass.
sentences.zh: 我们将尝试超越官方记录，跳出我们已经想到的要保存并放在博物馆玻璃柜里的东西。

sentences.en: Instead, we're going to talk to historians and writers and storytellers and just normal people about discarded objects and small personal keepsakes
sentences.zh: 相反，我们将与历史学家、作家、讲故事的人以及普通人谈论那些被丢弃的物品、小小的个人纪念品，

sentences.en: and all kinds of things that are so common we don't think about how important they really are.
sentences.zh: 以及各种各样太常见以至于我们忽略了它们真正重要性的东西。

sentences.en: We're going to see what stories those kinds of objects have to tell us about where we've been as a country.
sentences.zh: 我们将看看这些物品能告诉我们关于我们作为一个国家走过的历程。

sentences.en: The good and the bad.
sentences.zh: 好的和坏的。

sentences.en: The promises and the failures.
sentences.zh: 承诺和失败。

sentences.en: Jill LaForte, thank you so much for talking with me.
sentences.zh: 吉尔·莱波雷，非常感谢你与我交谈。

sentences.en: I really had a great time.
sentences.zh: 我真的很开心。

sentences.en: No, I had a great time too.
sentences.zh: 不，我也很开心。

sentences.en: I can't wait to see what you guys put in your safe.
sentences.zh: 我迫不及待想看看你们会在保险箱里放什么。

sentences.en: Whatever we put in our safe, it won't be a time capsule for the future.
sentences.zh: 无论我们放什么，它都不会是给未来的时间胶囊。

sentences.en: This is a collection for right now.
sentences.zh: 这是一个属于当下的收藏。

sentences.en: An ongoing weekly exhibit of the past to help us understand this moment.
sentences.zh: 一个持续进行的每周展览，通过过去来帮助我们理解当下。

sentences.en: And we need you.
sentences.zh: 我们需要你。

sentences.en: I want you to look in your attics and think back through your family histories and tell us what objects you think tell a bigger story of America.
sentences.zh: 我希望你们翻翻阁楼，回顾一下家族史，告诉我们你们认为哪些物品能讲述一个更大的美国故事。

sentences.en: Email us at 100objects at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 请发送电子邮件至 100objects@99pi.org。

sentences.en: It's going to take all of us forgotten nobodies to do this right.
sentences.zh: 我们需要所有像我们这样被遗忘的无名小卒共同努力才能做好这件事。

sentences.en: Join us as we make history.
sentences.zh: 加入我们，一起创造历史。

sentences.en: There was a version of this show back in 2010 from the BBC that was focused on the world.
sentences.zh: 2010年英国广播公司曾制作过一个版本的节目，关注的是全世界。

sentences.en: A history of the world in 100 objects.
sentences.zh: 《世界历史：100件物品》。

sentences.en: The stories all came from objects housed in the British Museum.
sentences.zh: 所有的故事都来自大英博物馆收藏的物品。

sentences.en: And I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢它。

sentences.en: It was a landmark show.
sentences.zh: 那是一个里程碑式的节目。

sentences.en: So I'm proud to be working with BBC Studios on this new and reimagined version.
sentences.zh: 所以我很自豪能与BBC工作室合作，制作这个全新的、重新构想的版本。

sentences.en: Picking up the mantle and telling stories about the USA.
sentences.zh: 接过接力棒，讲述关于美国的故事。

sentences.en: We'll be bringing you new episodes every Friday, right here in the 99% Invisible Fee.
sentences.zh: 我们每周五都会在这里为您带来新剧集，就在《99%无形》的订阅源里。

sentences.en: Our next episode will air next Friday.
sentences.zh: 下一集将于下周五播出。

sentences.en: But if you want to hear that episode and all future episodes one week early, subscribe to SiriusXM Podcast Plus.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想提前一周收听那一集以及所有未来的剧集，请订阅 SiriusXM Podcast Plus。

sentences.en: My guest, Jill Lepore, is a historian, professor of American history at Harvard University, and professor of law at Harvard Law School.
sentences.zh: 我的嘉宾吉尔·莱波雷是一位历史学家，哈佛大学美国历史教授，哈佛法学院法学教授。

sentences.en: She's also a staff writer at The New Yorker and a brand new recipient of the Pulitzer Prize.
sentences.zh: 她也是《纽约客》的特约撰稿人，还是普利策奖的新晋得主。

sentences.en: I love every single one of her books, but the jubilee edition of her amazing book, These Truths, A History of the United States, was just released.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢她的每一本书，但她那本精彩著作《这些真理：美国历史》的禧年版刚刚发布。

sentences.en: It's so good, guys.
sentences.zh: 真的太棒了，伙计们。

sentences.en: You gotta read it.
sentences.zh: 你们一定要读一读。

sentences.zh: 《美国历史百物志》由 99% Invisible 和 BBC Studios 联合制作。

sentences.zh: 由我 Roman Mars 担任主持和策划。

sentences.zh: 系列制片人为 Priscilla Alabi、Brenna Daldorf 和 Ellie Lightfoot。

sentences.zh: 助理制片人为 Isaac Fisher。

sentences.zh: BBC Studios 的执行制片人为 Annie Brown 和 Courtney Harrell。

sentences.zh: 艺术设计由 Stephan Lawrence 完成。

sentences.zh: 99% Invisible 是 Sirius XM 播客家族的一员，总部位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市美丽的住宅区。

sentences.zh: BBC Studios 总部位于伦敦西区美丽的白城。

sentences.zh: 如果您想与我们联系，或有建议我们考虑的物品，请发送电子邮件至 100objects@99pi.org。

sentences.zh: 感谢 Julian P.

sentences.zh: Cantor 收藏馆（位于 Carl Albert 中心档案馆）

sentences.zh: 以及 Gerald Ford 总统图书馆允许我们使用“世纪保险箱”开启时的音频。
